title: Christfox
html_source:
Lyster gets similar treatment to AE in Stephen’s internal narrative although there is a stronger structuralist element to this inner string of Stephen’s. Strucutralism is the placing of a story in the foundations of another, in this case what T.S. Elliott, impressed at Ulysses, called the Mythic Method (in so doing Joyce rescued art for the 20th century).

Nominally , Joyce placed Bloom’s day in the foundations of The Odyssey wishing to render it sub specie temporis nosrti (of our own time). There are other structuralist parallels (Garber.M, Shakespeare and Modern culture, p212):

man, son, wife are reproduced numerous times:

Ulysses, Telemachus, Penelope
Bloom, Stephen, Molly
Shakespeare, Hamnet Shakespeare, Ann Hathaway
Ghost, Hamlet, Gertrude
God, Christ, Mary.

Stephen looks at Lyster and thinks of the origin of the Quakers, George Fox,but for seven lines, his thoughts are a slurry of Fox, Christ and Shakespeare with strings of their relationships (above) attached.

This is the nub of modernism. The plot is dead, once aware of the meaning of the allusions in his thoughts, you experience the ache of his lost yearn for a father which of course is that of jj.
